planting.note: Plant tubers eye-up 4-6 inches deep after soil has warmed and frost danger has passed.

directions: Cryfield Harmony is a ball-form dahlia prized for its intense magenta-purple, precisely geometric blooms held on long, strong stems. The tightly arranged petals radiate outward in near-perfect globe symmetry, making it a reliable exhibition and cut-flower variety. Stake plants early since the tall stems carry heavy flower heads, and pinch the central growing tip to encourage branching and more bloom. Deadhead spent flowers regularly to keep the plant producing from midsummer through the first frosts.

planting.note: Plant tubers eye-up 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed; part of the Wootton series of English-raised show dahlias.

directions: Wootton Impact produces light bronze-yellow, globe-shaped flowers roughly 6 inches across on long, sturdy stems well suited to cutting. As part of the Wootton series of English-bred show dahlias, it combines a dependable ball form with an unusual warm bronze-gold tone. Stake plants at transplanting to support the tall stems and heavy flower heads, and pinch the growing tip early to build a well-branched plant. Regular deadheading keeps new buds forming through the season.

common_name: Golden Scepter Dahlia (Historic Golden-Yellow Pompon Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers eye-up 4-6 inches deep after soil has warmed; a Dutch-bred pompon variety dating to the 1920s still grown for cutting.

directions: Golden Scepter is a historic Dutch pompon dahlia, nearly a century old, that forms perfectly round, tightly quilled golden-yellow blooms about 3 inches across that warm to a soft peach tone as they age. Its small, perfectly spherical flowers and sturdy stems make it a favorite for cutting gardens and mixed bouquets. Pinch young plants to encourage branching and more flowering stems, and deadhead spent blooms to extend the long June-through-October flowering season. Divide and store tubers over winter in cold climates to carry this long-lived heirloom variety forward.

common_name: Joe Swift Dahlia (White Single-Flowered Dahlia with Bronze Foliage)

planting.note: Plant tubers eye-up 4-6 inches deep after soil has warmed; a compact single-flowered dahlia bred in the UK.

directions: Joe Swift bears single, yellow-centered white flowers that take on soft pink blush as they age, set against dark bronze-green foliage that makes the blooms pop by contrast. Its open, single-petaled flower form is especially attractive to bees and other pollinators throughout the summer. Grow in full sun in rich, well-drained soil, pinching young plants to build a bushier habit before flowering begins. Deadhead regularly to keep fresh buds coming from midsummer until the first frosts.

common_name: Twyning's Candy Dahlia (Crimson and White Striped Single Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers eye-up 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed; an RHS Award of Garden Merit single-flowered dahlia.

directions: Twyning's Candy produces striking single flowers with broad, flat crimson florets, each marked by a bold central white stripe surrounding a deep yellow disc. The candy-striped petals and open single form make it a strong pollinator plant as well as a distinctive border and container dahlia. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil, pinching the growing tip early to encourage a bushier, more floriferous plant. This variety holds the RHS Award of Garden Merit for its reliable garden performance from midsummer through the first frosts.

common_name: Happy Single Party Dahlia (Bright Yellow Single Dahlia with Bronze Foliage)

planting.note: Plant tubers eye-up 4-6 inches deep after soil has warmed; part of the compact Happy Single series bred for bedding and containers.

directions: Happy Single Party bears bright yellow single flowers with a contrasting brown-black center, held above dark bronze-purple foliage on a compact, well-branched plant. As part of the Happy Single series, it was bred for garden and container performance rather than exhibition, flowering continuously from early summer into fall. The open single blooms are highly attractive to bees and other pollinators. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil and deadhead regularly to keep the compact plants flowering heavily.

common_name: Natal Dahlia (Old-Fashioned Velvety Red Ball Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers eye-up 4-6 inches deep after soil has warmed; a long-grown heirloom ball dahlia.

directions: Natal is an old-fashioned ball dahlia producing deep, velvety dark-red flowers about 3 inches across on sturdy stems, a long-cultivated heirloom variety still valued for cutting. Its compact ball form and rich color have kept it in circulation among heirloom bulb growers for decades. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil, pinching young plants to encourage branching before the main flush of bloom. Deadhead through the season to keep the plant producing from midsummer until frost.
